bibliography.note: Crossref: J. Freshwater Ecology 34(1): 771–782, doi:10.1080/02705060.2019.1687109; title as cited. The stand-in is Penney, H. D. 2019. Environmental and maternal effects on hatch characteristics and early growth of fishes in Newfoundland and Labrador. PhD thesis, Memorial University of Newfoundland, St. John's (Chapter 2: 'Abiotic factors at a range edge constrains reproduction in an ectotherm').

claims.note: Article not read. The thesis supports it: p. 31 (PDF p. 48), 22 °C 'mean: 274.4 ATU, sd: 12.9; days mean: 12.5 sd:0.6'; 8.3 d at 28 °C, 21.0 d at 16 °C (n = 34 hatched in all). Conditions: laboratory, single embryos in Petri dishes, collected 24 June–11 July 2014 on spawning mops in Burton's Pond, St. John's, NL (an introduced population).

Article not read. The thesis supports it with a condition: p. 32 (PDF p. 49), standard length on hatch day 'mean 7.1 mm, sd:0.2' in four of the five treatment combinations that hatched. At 28 °C and 0.6 mS/cm hatchlings were 6.4 mm SL (sd 0.2), significantly smaller.

claims.claim: banded killifish eggs need warmth: none hatched at 10 °C, at most 10 % at 16 °C and more than 74 % at 22–28 °C (via a thesis)
claims.note: Article not read. The thesis supports it: pp. 30–31 (PDF pp. 47–48). No embryos hatched in either 10 °C treatment, 22 and 28 °C gave 'reasonable hatch success (>74%)', and the two 16 °C treatments gave 'very low hatch success (0 and 10%)'. Conditions: 107 embryos, 4 temperatures × 2 conductivities (0.6, 1.2 mS/cm), only 2 embryos hatched at 16 °C. The authors infer a threshold between 16 and 22 °C (p. 33).

notes: Stand-in: Penney 2019 PhD thesis (MUN), Chapter 2. It supports all three uses, with the conditions above. The paper already says 'via a thesis', so cite the thesis itself (Penney 2019, PhD thesis, Memorial University of Newfoundland, ch. 2), or have the human open the OA article (doi:10.1080/02705060.2019.1687109) and check that the published numbers did not change from the thesis chapter, which was then 'under consideration'. Also in the thesis: the documented spawning range is given as '19-24°C (Chippett, 2004)' (p. 27, PDF p. 44) and the optimal development range as 'between 19 and 24°C (Chippett 2004)' (p. 33). The paper's Table 3.6-1 gives 19–23 °C for Chippett (via COSEWIC 2014); check that against Chippett. Newfoundland vs Maritimes: about 1,000 vs over 1,700 °C thermal units above 15 °C by the end of October (air temperature, 2010–17).
